ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus speciosus* reaches 70 mm SVL. It features a grey-brown body with distinct dark-edged, pale yellow spots and a slender, curved tail. It is distinguished by its lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus speciosus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of dark, light-edged blotches along the vertebral line, lacking the transverse bands seen in similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus speciosus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks or rocks at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Forest Spotted Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects and small invertebrates among the leaf litter and low vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus speciosus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus speciosus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
